Over the past generations, whether you need to buy Apple's largest iPhone Pro to get the top-tier camera features has varied. Until now, most reports have indicated that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max should have the same camera specs, but today a leaker has cast some doubt on that.

Specifically, he said that two new features originally expected on both Pro models "may" become exclusive to the Pro Max…

The iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max have identical camera specs, with three rear lenses all being 48-megapixel sensors. Apple says the telephoto lens offers up to 8x optical zoom, but this is actually achieved by cropping a 24-megapixel image, so it's more accurate to say it has 4x optical zoom and offers an 8x cropped image option.

We've so far (broadly) expected this year's Pro models to maintain identical camera specs, with both featuring a variable aperture main lens and a larger aperture telephoto lens, the latter for better performance in low light.

However, leaker Ice Universe says the two new telephoto lens features may be exclusive to the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

If this turns out to be true, it means you'd have to buy the Pro Max to get the longest telephoto zoom and the best low-light photography. However, he used the word "may," which suggests he's not entirely sure about this claim himself, possibly having seen conflicting evidence within Apple's supply chain.

There's also been talk that the variable aperture system on the main lens may be exclusive to the Pro Max, but reports on that have varied.

If you normally prefer the smaller of the two Pro models, would this situation make you upgrade to the Pro Max for the better camera features? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
